heading: Why IT Workers Face Special Pressure

rows: Bank staffer checks an ex's balance

Can ✓ — should ✗: snooping, not an authorised task
Support tech copies a customer's photos
Remote control opens all their files
Can ✓ — should ✗: touch only what fixes the fault
Developer keeps a copy of employer's source

heading: Relationship 1 — the Employer
title: Loyalty & honesty to the employer — breaches and their fallout
rows: Copied client source code for a weekend side gig
IP theft; betrays employer AND client
Listed a CCNA on the CV without holding it
Installed pirated AutoCAD 'to cut costs' on orders
Legal liability for the firm AND the installer
Moonlighted for the employer's direct rival
Judgment serves two masters — trust lost
Leaked the internal client list to a friend's startup
Confidential asset gone; possible legal action
Inflated hours on a project timesheet
Billing fraud; erodes the employer's trust
note: Loyalty and honesty are the two duties; each row shows one being broken — and 'the boss ordered it' never transfers the blame off you.

heading: Relationship 2 — the Client
title: When the client can't check — asymmetry exploited (Nepal / IT)
headers: Why the client couldn't catch it
rows: Sold an NGO an over-sized ERP it didn't need
They can't judge what capacity they actually need
No technical staff to test the code before paying
Hid that the portal can't handle election-day load
Load only shows up in production, months later
Used cheap unlicensed libraries without saying
Client can't read the dependency list
Left no documentation, to lock in future work
They don't know documentation was owed
Quietly stored client data on a free foreign host
Invisible unless a leak exposes it
note: Every breach survives only because of information asymmetry — the client cannot verify until it's too late. That is why the duty is professional, not just contractual.

heading: Is IT a 'Profession'?
title: Profession or not? — fields against the four-part test (Nepal)
rows: Yes — NMC licenses and can strike off
Yes — must be enrolled to practise
No licence to build banking software
Partial — has knowledge + codes, no licensing
Not a profession — anyone can claim the title
note: The single differentiator is self-regulation — a licence you can lose. IT has education, knowledge and codes but no strike-off, so it is a partial profession.

heading: Professional Codes of Ethics
title: Applying the code — an ask, the principle, the answer
headers: What the code says to do
rows: Build hidden user tracking without consent
Ship now with a known security hole
Avoid harm; be honest about limits
Disclose the risk; don't hide it
Claim a system is more secure than it is
State the real capabilities to the client
Reuse a rival's leaked source code
Refuse — it isn't yours to use
Quietly weaken data protection to cut cost
Push back; protect the user's data
Blame a junior for your own bug
note: A code is only useful when applied to a concrete ask — and it hands you professional language to say no, even without a government licence behind it.

heading: Licensing & Professional Organizations
title: Who grants it? — real credentials & bodies classified
note: The test that sorts every row: WHO grants it, and does it carry LEGAL FORCE? Only government-granted items are licences.

heading: Software Piracy
title: Is it piracy? — everyday cases (Nepal / IT)
rows: Office runs cracked Windows on every PC
Piracy — no valid licence, even unsold
Shop sells 'original' Windows DVDs that are fake
A 5-seat design licence used by 50 staff
Installing one cracked Photoshop for yourself
Piracy — no sale needed to violate
Downloading a 'nulled' paid plugin to save money
Piracy — using value you never paid for
Buying one Windows key, reusing it on 10 laptops
note: None of these require a sale — the wrong is USING value you never paid for. 'Everyone does it' is the Unit 1 normalization trap, not a defence.

heading: Data Privacy
title: Privacy principle broken — everyday data grabs (Nepal)
rows: SIM dealer sells your number to loan marketers
A flood of unsolicited loan calls
Loan-form data reused to target you with ads
Mall QR form demands your citizenship number
Bank KYC records leak to a data broker
An app asks for contacts it doesn't need
Clinic shares its patient list with a pharmacy
note: Nepal's Individual Privacy Act 2075 recognises these rights; the gap is enforcement. Privacy is control, not secrecy — each row is control taken away.

heading: Surveillance
title: Monitoring or spying? — same tech, disclosure decides
rows: Employer logs email, stated in a signed AUP
Boss secretly installs a keylogger on your PC
CCTV at a bank entrance with visible signage
Hidden camera in a staff changing room
ISP logs traffic per a disclosed policy
Manager reads staff personal DMs 'to be safe'
note: The technology is identical row to row — transparency and consent (the S8 AUP clause) plus proportionality are what shift it from spying to monitoring.

heading: Anonymity Online
title: Anonymity's two edges — the same cover, opposite uses
rows: Asks for support without being traced
Panics the public with no accountability
note: Any rule that silences the bottom three also silences the top three — which is why real-name registration is contested. And true anonymity is rare: logs and metadata leave a trail.

heading: Why Social Networking Is an Ethics Hotspot
title: Amplifiers in action — small act, mass harm (Nepal)
rows: A doctored celebrity screenshot posted once
A fake 'bank X is collapsing' clip
Said what they'd never say face-to-face
An outrage post the algorithm boosts
Thousands watch a pile-on, no one steps in
Silence reads as approval; harm grows
A false earthquake rumour forwarded 'to warn'
note: These are Unit 1's scale/speed/permanence factors made personal — and online harm carries real legal, social and psychological consequences.

heading: Fake News & Misinformation
title: Mis- or dis-information? — classify the share (Nepal)
rows: Forwarding a fake health cure you believed
A staged rumour planted to sway an election
Sharing an old photo as 'today's flood'
A scam page inventing a fake lottery win
Coordinated fake reviews to destroy a rival
note: The only difference is intent — but you are responsible either way, because the share button is an act that scales the lie.
